szoveg_eredeti:
Systematic Review Evaluates Artificial Intelligence and Expert Systems in Date Palm Agriculture

A comprehensive systematic review investigating precision agriculture in arid ecosystems has evaluated thirty-nine peer-reviewed studies published between January 2020 and October 2024 to determine how artificial intelligence and expert systems are transforming date palm cultivation. Date palms serve as an essential agricultural and cultural cornerstone across arid and semi-arid territories, with Saudi Arabia standing as the world’s second largest producer of palm dates. Despite increasing deployment of automated technologies to monitor orchards, previous scientific literature remained highly fragmented, lacking a unified synthesis of domain-specific machine learning architectures, sensor configurations, and decision-support platforms tailored to the crop.

The review followed the structured Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses guidelines, utilizing the Kuwait University Library discovery platform to query five major research databases: Scopus, Web of Science, SpringerLink, ScienceDirect, and IEEE. The search strategy combined Boolean terms covering date palm cultivation, expert systems, decision-support tools, machine learning, and specific operational domains including disease diagnosis, fertilization, and climatic impacts. From the initial screening, duplicate citations, non-peer-reviewed manuscripts, non-English publications, and studies examining unrelated species such as oil palm were excluded. The final corpus comprised thirty-nine eligible investigations, with journal articles accounting for 89.7 percent of the analyzed literature and conference proceedings representing the remaining 10.3 percent. Quality assessments conducted across ten standardized checklist metrics revealed that one study attained high quality, thirty-three were classified as average quality, and five fell into the low-quality bracket.

Across the identified computational frameworks, deep learning architectures emerged as the predominant methodology, implemented in sixteen studies, or 64 percent of the reviewed research. Convolutional neural networks represented the core engine for image-based visual recognition, leveraging alternating convolutional layers, pooling operations, and fully connected layers to extract hierarchical topological patterns directly from agricultural inputs without requiring manual feature engineering. Pretrained models and transfer learning paradigms were deployed across six studies, representing 24 percent of the reviewed corpus. Notably, specialized architectures such as the DPXception model adapted a pretrained Xception backbone to classify four distinct date palm species, surpassing standard baselines including ResNet50 and EfficientNet. Transfer learning also proved effective when deploying MobileNetV2, an architecture utilizing inverted residuals and linear bottlenecks to perform rapid classification on resource-constrained embedded field equipment.

Beyond standard convolutional frameworks, researchers increasingly adopted diverse machine learning models and sequential neural networks to handle structured agricultural metrics. Tree-based ensemble methods, notably Random Forest and Extreme Gradient Boosting, appeared in seven investigations, representing 28 percent of the analyzed papers. Random Forest models demonstrated high predictive consistency for date fruit evaluation by aggregating predictions across numerous randomized decision trees, while gradient boosted ensembles effectively predicted disease outbreaks, fruit quality, and overall production yields. Statistical and linear models appeared in five studies, addressing continuous variables such as water consumption and ambient meteorological impacts. Support vector machines and support vector regression accounted for four studies, mapping inputs into higher-dimensional spaces via kernel functions to resolve complex non-linear agricultural interactions. Recurrent neural networks, specifically Long Short-Term Memory models, were utilized to evaluate time-series sequences, using gating mechanisms to govern memory cells for precise irrigation demand projections.

The analyzed investigations addressed several primary operational domains, led by date fruit quality evaluation and post-harvest management across twelve studies, alongside disease diagnosis and pest management across eleven studies. Crop monitoring and canopy assessment constituted seven studies, while agricultural irrigation management was explored in five investigations. Genetic analysis and sustainable energy utilization remained comparatively sparse, appearing in three studies and one study, respectively. In disease and pest surveillance, deep learning achieved high classification performance, exceeding 90 percent accuracy in multiple trials and reaching up to 99.62 percent in specialized leaf illness identification tasks. For example, support vector machine classifiers reached 98.29 percent accuracy when differentiating developmental stages of white scale disease, while convolutional neural network frameworks processing acoustic signals recorded from date palm foliage successfully segregated pest-damaged tissues from healthy samples, demonstrating non-invasive detection capabilities.

Expert systems formed a second major technological pillar within the synthesized corpus, incorporating rule-based decision trees, multivariate regressions, spatial modeling, and analytical laboratory instrumentation. Fourteen studies detailed expert system architectures designed to simulate specialist decision-making through dedicated knowledge bases, logical inference engines, and operator user interfaces. In physical monitoring applications, researchers integrated Response Surface Methodology to mathematically optimize processing conditions, while matrix-assisted laser desorption ionization-time-of-flight mass spectrometry precisely profiled bacterial protein expressions to optimize silage production from date palm leaves. For broader spatial and ecological forecasting, hybrid Cellular Automata and Markov Chain models were implemented to simulate spatial land-use transitions, projecting an expansion of date palm plantations across Algeria’s Ziban agricultural region with an overall simulation accuracy of 88 percent.

The physical sensing infrastructure described across the reviewed literature revealed sophisticated instrumentation interfacing with embedded processing hardware. Ground installations incorporated relative humidity and temperature sensors, such as DHT22 and RHT10 units, to evaluate canopy microclimates and project environmental plant stress. Soil moisture monitoring utilized capacitive and resistive transducers to monitor volumetric water content, establishing baseline voltages to optimize deficit irrigation schedules. Load cells amplified by HX711 converters tracked real-time gravimetric weight shifts to assess crop water uptake and fruit yield, while flow sensors regulated distribution valves. For post-harvest storage, ultrasonic transducers vibrating at 2600 kilohertz successfully atomized coating solutions to extend the fresh preservation period of harvested date fruits up to 65 days. Satellite remote sensing deployments integrated multispectral IKONOS, Landsat-8, and WorldView-2 data, attaining classification accuracies up to 94.5 percent when mapping mature, medium, and young palms across large growing territories.

Despite strong reported benchmark results, the systematic review identified critical technical limitations across the current literature regarding data diversity, operational deployment, and generalizability. A substantial 48 percent of the reviewed AI studies relied on small datasets containing fewer than 1000 samples, which sharply elevates the probability of statistical overfitting and limits model reliability when deployed outside controlled settings.
